sections.h2: What one link actually costs, and why ₹1,000 is a liability
body: Almost nobody in Indian SEO will tell you what a single link costs them to produce. It's the most useful number in the whole discipline, so here's ours.

None of these figures is a payment to the publisher. We don't buy do-follow links — that's a direct violation of Google's link spam policy, and the difference between [paid links and earned links](/compare/paid-links-vs-earned-links) tends to surface in a core update two years later, when you've forgotten you agreed to it. What you're paying for is research, a pitch worth reading, an asset worth linking to, and the eleven follow-ups that produce one yes.

callout.title: Cheap links aren't a bargain, they're a debt
callout.body: A bad link doesn't just fail to help. It sits in your profile until an algorithm update decides what to do with it, and the disavow-and-recover work later costs more than the good links would have. We've never met a founder who regretted buying fewer links.

sections.h2: You approve every domain before we send an email
body: This is the part most agencies won't do, because it slows them down and it exposes the quality of their target list. It's also the only thing that stops your brand appearing on a site you'd be embarrassed by.
The flow is the same every month.
numbered: **We build a scored prospect list.** Relevance to your sector first, then traffic and link profile, then whether the site has ever published anything a human read. You get the sheet.
**You veto.** Strike any domain, no reason needed. Competitors, ex-employers, that publication that ran a bad piece about your category — all fair. Most clients strike three to five.
**We write the asset and pitch it.** You see the pitch template before it goes out, and the full email thread is in the shared folder if you ever want to read it.

**The link goes live and we send you the URL.** Live URL, anchor text, the page it points at, and the link attribute — do-follow, nofollow or sponsored. All three get reported. We don't quietly count nofollows as wins.
**Monthly report.** New referring domains this month, cumulative count against your day-one baseline, and what died in outreach and why.

callout.title: The one-question test for any link vendor
callout.body: Ask to see last month's live URLs for another client, with the client's permission. An agency doing real work has that file open in ten seconds. An agency buying links will explain why it's confidential.

sections.h2: The four things we won't do, even if you ask
body: We've lost pitches over this list. That's the trade.
bullets: **Private blog networks.** A PBN is a set of domains someone owns for the sole purpose of linking to clients. Every one of them eventually gets deindexed as a group, and everything they pointed at goes with them. "Our own network" and "we have relationships with 500 sites" mean the same thing.
**Link farms and mass directory submission.** Two thousand links from sites with no readers doesn't look like authority. It looks like a signature.
**Sitewide footer and blogroll links.** One paid footer link on a 40,000-page site is 40,000 identical links with identical anchor text. It reads as exactly what it is.

**Paid do-follow placements without disclosure.** If money changes hands, the link should carry `rel="sponsored"`. Plenty of Indian publications will sell you a do-follow anyway. We'll tell you the price they quoted and then decline for you.

callout.title: The arithmetic nobody does out loud
callout.body: On a ₹75,000/mo SEO retainer, links take roughly 20–30% — call it ₹15,000–₹22,500. At our published costs that's one to two real placements a month. If a vendor is promising twenty at that price, one of the two numbers is fiction, and it isn't the price.

sections.h2: What we guarantee, and the thing no one can
body: Our company guarantee is about leads, not links: we freeze your trailing-90-day qualified leads from organic search on day one, and if we haven't beaten that number in 90 days we keep working free until we do. That's the promise on every [SEO engagement](/seo).

On link building specifically we add a second frozen number — your referring-domain count on day one — and commit to a monthly target against it, in writing, from the table above. You'll know by month two whether we're hitting it, because the live URLs are in the report.

What we will never do is guarantee a ranking position. Not first, not top three, not "page one in 90 days". Nobody controls Google's index, Google's own guidelines warn against exactly this promise, and an agency that makes it is either buying links or planning to be somewhere else when it doesn't land.
Full pricing, including where SEO starts for smaller sites, is on the [pricing page](/pricing).

faqs.q: How much do link building services cost in India?
faqs.a: Real placements cost ₹8,000–₹25,000 each in work, depending on the publication. Agencies package that as a retainer: ₹25,000–₹45,000 a month buys 2–4 new referring domains for a young site, ₹75,000+ buys 6–12 for an established brand. Anything advertised under ₹5,000 a month is buying links, not earning them.

No. Paying for a do-follow link violates Google's link spam policy, and the risk lands on your domain, not ours. If a publication quotes us a price for coverage, we'll forward you the quote and decline it. Where a paid placement genuinely makes commercial sense as advertising, it gets a sponsored attribute and we don't count it as a link win.

faqs.q: How long before backlinks affect rankings?
faqs.a: Google has to crawl the linking page, then reassess the target page. That's typically weeks, not days, and the effect compounds over months rather than landing at once. Expect to see impressions move for the linked page within 4–8 weeks of a good placement, and expect a single link to rarely be the reason anything ranks.

faqs.q: What's the difference between guest posting and digital PR?
faqs.a: Guest posting means you write the article and the site publishes it, usually because a relationship or a fee exists. Digital PR means a journalist writes about you because you gave them something worth writing about. The second is harder, costs more per attempt, and produces links you can't buy. See [guest posting versus digital PR](/compare/guest-posting-vs-digital-pr).

faqs.q: Can I do link building myself?
faqs.a: The highest-value link work is genuinely in-house: your customers, suppliers, partners, industry bodies and the trade press already know you. A founder's email gets a reply an agency's doesn't. Where agencies earn the fee is volume, prospecting at scale, and building assets people want to cite. Start with your own network before you pay anyone.

faqs.q: How do I know if my current backlinks are hurting me?
faqs.a: Look for sudden spikes in referring domains you didn't earn, anchor text stuffed with commercial keywords, links from sites in unrelated languages or sectors, and footer links across whole domains. Any of those and it's worth a toxic-link audit before you spend another rupee on new links.
